Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating Clara Davies, a 40-year-old accountant who attended my clinic regarding longstanding musculoskeletal and cutaneous concerns. She takes daily over-the-counter vitamin D, does not smoke, and has an unremarkable family history.

Her difficulties began in early infancy, when her parents first noted that her skin would tear and split following trivial shearing friction. Throughout her life, she has experienced marked ecchymoses from negligible contact, with minor cuts reliably healing into depressed, paper-thin, parchment-like scars, particularly across her pretibial regions and elbows. 

On physical examination, her vital signs are normal, with a heart rate of 72 bpm and blood pressure of 118/76 mmHg. Her integument feels unusually velvety and dough-like to palpation, and she displays pronounced cutaneous stretchability, with skin on her volar forearms extending easily well past expected thresholds before promptly recoiling. Articular examination reveals widespread, prominent joint laxity affecting both large and small joints symmetrically. 

A review of systems is largely negative; she denies any history of recurrent chest infections, repeated pneumonias, or chronic cough. Her cranial nerve exam, baseline hematology, and renal panels were entirely within normal limits. 

I would be very grateful for your comprehensive clinical assessment and guidance regarding ongoing management for this patient.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Sterling
